comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C13-C17 regarding species-specific salt preferences. Both evaluations find the behavioral chemotaxis data well-supported and accept the findings without critique.

Perfect agreement on claims C24-C27 regarding che-1 mutant and silencing phenotypes. Both accept the behavioral data demonstrating ASE function in salt chemotaxis, though OpenEval notes the unexplained discrepancy between mutant and silencing results for NH4I.

Agreement on claims C42-C43 but with different perspectives. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to the puzzling disconnect between calcium imaging defects and behavioral phenotypes in gcy-22.3 mutants. Peer reviewers accept the finding as SUPPORTED, treating it as evidence of redundancy/compensation without expressing concern about the contradiction.

Strong agreement on claims C28-C33 regarding ASEL/R functional asymmetry. Both evaluations praise the calcium imaging data showing lateralized responses. Peer review also includes C3 (not in OpenEval R4) and explicitly highlights the convincing evidence for lateralization.

Strong agreement on claims C11, C12, C44, C69 regarding lsy-6-independent asymmetry establishment. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. Peer review explicitly highlights this as a key contribution showing alternative evolutionary mechanisms, while noting the actual pathway remains uncharacterized.

Agreement on claims C34-C36 regarding AFD biphasic salt responses. Both find the calcium imaging data SUPPORTED. Peer review additionally includes C60 (AFD-ASER connectivity) which OpenEval addresses separately in R12.

Agreement on claims C47-C49 regarding species-specific differences in salt sensing. Both find the comparative analysis SUPPORTED. Peer review also includes C53 (concentration-dependent responses) which OpenEval addresses separately in R11.

Agreement on claims C18-C20, C68 regarding che-1 expression patterns. Both find the reporter and endogenous tagging data SUPPORTED. OpenEval R2 additionally includes C22-C23 (autoregulation and ttx-1 co-localization) not mentioned in peer review R3.

Agreement on claims C39-C41 regarding gcy-22.3 mutant calcium imaging phenotypes. Both find the data SUPPORTED. Peer review R5 additionally includes C37-C38 (gcy-22.3 expression) which OpenEval addresses separately in R6.

Partial overlap on gcy-22.3 characterization. OpenEval R6 focuses on claims C37-C38 (expression and che-1 regulation) rated SUPPORTED. Peer review R5 includes these claims along with C39-C41 (functional data), all rated SUPPORTED.

Disagreement on claim C64 regarding che-1 function. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether che-1 truly functions as a terminal selector based on phenotypic discrepancies. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN but focuses on the uncharacterized downstream pathway rather than questioning che-1's role itself.

Partial overlap on claim C71 regarding miRNA pathway conservation. OpenEval rates C71-C73 as UNCERTAIN, noting that speculation about lability requires more data. Peer review R10 addresses C64 and C71 together, rating UNCERTAIN due to uncharacterized mechanisms.

Minimal overlap on claim C60 regarding AFD-ASER connectivity. OpenEval R12 addresses C50 and C60 as SUPPORTED inferences from calcium imaging and behavioral data. Peer review R7 includes C60 with C34-C36 (AFD responses), all rated SUPPORTED.

Minimal overlap on claim C53 regarding concentration-dependent responses. OpenEval R11 addresses C53-C55 as SUPPORTED with appropriate caveats about calcium indicator differences. Peer review R9 includes C53 with C47-C49 (species differences), all rated SUPPORTED.
OpenEval addresses claims C67, C66 regarding independent gcy gene duplication events, rating as SUPPORTED based on genomic data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
